name: ROSAT
summary: Historical German–US–UK soft-X-ray and extreme-ultraviolet astronomy satellite, operating from 1990 to 1999. ROSAT hot-gas imaging provided evidence for gravitational potentials and dark-matter halos in galaxies and groups, and survey archives for later cosmology. Included here for gravity and structure research, without claiming observation of particle-dark-matter X-ray decay.
physics_targets: Total gravitational mass of galaxy groups and clusters
Spatial distributions of dark and visible matter
detection_principle: A grazing-incidence X-ray telescope with PSPC or HRI measures hot-gas surface brightness and morphology. Models of gas in a gravitational potential, together with temperature or optical distributions, infer total mass and dark matter. This differs from searches for photons produced by dark-matter annihilation / decay.

status.label: Mission ended; historical archive available
status.evidence: NASA HEASARC lists a mission lifetime of 1990-06-01 to 1999-02-12 and provides historical data products.

timeline.event: Launched and began an all-sky survey, followed by pointed observations.
PSPC observed hot gas in the NGC2300 galaxy group, supplying data for mass inference.
NGC720 geometric dark-matter study submitted as a preprint; published the following year.

collaboration.name: ROSAT German / US / UK mission partnership
lead_institutions: Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics
collaboration.participants_note: Joint German–US–UK mission. Dark-matter geometry studies were analyses by astronomers using ROSAT data, not a separate dedicated dark-matter collaboration.

key_parameters.name: X-ray energy band
key_parameters.value: 0.1–2.5 keV, according to the HEASARC mission page

key_parameters.name: PSPC field of view and effective area
key_parameters.value: About 2° diameter; about 240 cm² at 1 keV

phases.name: All-sky survey
phases.description: About the first six months of the mission, using PSPC; produced RASS.

phases.name: Pointed observations
phases.description: Deep exposures after the all-sky survey, including hot-gas studies of galaxies and groups.

phases.name: Data reanalysis
phases.description: HEASARC preserves catalogs, spectra, light curves, images and raw data.

results.summary: Using PSPC images of NGC720, Buote and Canizares found that mass following optical light alone could not reproduce the X-ray isophotes, providing geometric evidence for dark matter under their gas and gravity modeling assumptions.

NASA describes additional gravitational mass inferred from hot gas in the NGC2300 group. “Dark matter found” in the news title refers to gravitational evidence, not discovery of dark-matter particles.

science_scope: Astrophysical research on dark-matter distributions and gravitational evidence. No independent ROSAT sterile-neutrino or dark-matter decay-line search was verified in this review, so particle limits from other X-ray missions are not assigned to ROSAT.

uncertainties: Gravitational-mass inference from soft-X-ray-emitting hot gas depends on gas state, geometry and gravity models; it does not identify particles.
This dossier is primarily classified as cosmology_structure. Being an X-ray satellite does not automatically make it a particle indirect-detection experiment.
ROSAT galaxy-cluster mass studies and later archive-based cosmology have not been exhaustively covered.
Historical orbital map coordinates and specific image permissions have not been verified.
